text:
sarah: heads-up — after today's merge (inflight-prefetch change) we're seeing OOMs on longctx runs in staging. First repro around 3198765200. /cc @matt @anika

matt: copy. linked the failing job: https://ci/internal/jobs/319876 shows mem regression in kv_cache_longctx_mem.

ci-bot: FAILED: perf/regression kv_cache_longctx_mem (threshold +28%) — artifacts at https://ci/internal/artifacts/319876/flame.svg

anika: did a quick pprof on the failing instance. Top shows slab fragmentation: many small slabs (~3-8kb) are pinned. Hot allocation path points to kernel_router::select_kernel -> prefetch::reserve_inflight -> kv_cache_pin.

matt: that's suspicious — the inflight-prefetch change moved reservation earlier in the pipeline. It may now hold KV frames across batch boundaries.

sarah: paste from the node logs:
```
[2026-03-17T09:12:03Z] OOM killer invoked: rss=120GB kv_cache_used=98GB slab_free=2GB
alloc_trace: prefetch_reserve+0x84 -> kv_cache_pin -> slab_alloc
stack: kernel_router::route -> select_kernel -> prefetch::reserve_inflight
```

anika: also noticed the batching heuristic tweak in the same PR: batcher now groups by estimated token_active instead of strict model_shard. That caused more cross-seqlen coalescing in practice.

lee: cross-seqlen coalescing + early prefetch reservation sounds like a perfect fragmentation amplifier: long prompts keep many small hot slabs pinned while short prompts churn others -> overall free slab pool goes to zero.

matt: starting a local bisect across the PR range. Repro is fairly fast if you simulate mixed seq-length load (64/2048) with batch_size=8.

sarah: @deploy-bot please hold rollout for release-2026.03.17 — reason: kv memory regression triage. :exclamation:

deploy-bot: Rollout HELD: release-2026.03.17 — reason: "kv memory regression triage in progress" — eng-runtime notified.

matt: minimal repro found: mixed seq_len workload triggers mem climb to OOM when prefetch enabled. With prefetch disabled memory stays stable.

anika: proposal: (1) delay inflight reservation until after select_kernel (move reserve after kernel selection), (2) tighten batching grouping so we avoid coalescing sequences with >1.5x length ratio. Both cheap changes.

sarah: can we hotfix by reverting the inflight-prefetch change for the release? It's the fastest mitigation.

matt: I'll open a revert PR and also a targeted fix PR. Add a regression test to perf suite (mixed_seq_burst) that reproduces the scenario.

anika: also suggest CI add a pprof snapshot hook when kv mem increases >15% over baseline so future frag regressions fail fast.

sarah: plan: matt -> revert PR, anika -> post-merge fix + CI test, run canary on small fleet, then unhold if pass. Update this thread with results.

lee: storing notes and bisect steps here: https://wiki/internal/bisect/319876 (will paste bisect commit ranges).

sarah: thanks all — please keep updates short here.

matt: PR opened: #4832 revert(inflight-prefetch) — CI queued.

ci-bot: CI: perf/regression still failing on current head. Will re-run on revert-branch when available.

sarah: leaving rollout hold until canary confirms mem stability. If revert passes canary we resume.

deploy-bot: Noted. Rollout remains HELD until further notice.
